meta.title: Best BitLocker for Mac (2026): Honest Comparison of 6 Options
meta.description: Which BitLocker for Mac option fits you? Unbit, iBoysoft, Hasleo, UUByte, anylinuxfs and a Windows VM compared on price, write support, Apple silicon and setup. Updated October 2026.
meta.ogTitle: Best BitLocker for Mac (2026) – honest comparison

lead: macOS can’t open BitLocker-encrypted drives by itself, so you need a tool. There are several, and the best one depends on a single question: do you only need to read your files, or also write to the drive? This roundup compares six ways to do it, with the trade-offs spelled out.
disclosure: Disclosure: we make Unbit, one of the options below. We have tried to be fair. Unbit is read-only by design, so for some jobs another option is the better pick, and we say which. Facts about other products come from their vendors’ own pages (linked from each comparison page) and can change.

quick.title: The short answer
items: **Just need to read your files and copy them off the drive:** [Unbit](home) – free, read-only, no drivers.
**Need to write to BitLocker drives from your Mac:** a paid app such as iBoysoft BitLocker for Mac, Hasleo BitLocker Anywhere or UUByte BitLocker Geeker – or use Windows.
**Comfortable with Terminal on an Apple silicon Mac:** anylinuxfs – free, open source, read-write.
**Already run Windows in a virtual machine:** use Windows’ own BitLocker there, for example in Parallels Desktop.

how.title: How we chose
intro: We looked at the ways people actually open BitLocker drives on a Mac and kept the ones that have a vendor page or repository we could check. We compared them on what matters when the drive is in front of you:
criteria: **Does it do the job?** Open an encrypted external drive on macOS with a password or a recovery key.
**Read-only or read-write.** Writing is useful, but it also means the tool can change your drive.
**Price model.** Free, subscription or one-time licence.
**Apple silicon.** Whether it supports M-series Macs, not only Intel.
**Setup and system access.** Whether it needs system or kernel extensions, lowered startup security, Terminal or a virtual machine.
**Privacy and documentation.** Where decryption happens and how well the vendor explains setup.
outro: We did not run speed tests and we don’t give a numbered ranking, because the right choice depends on your job. Other tools exist; leaving one out is not a judgement on it. If you spot an error, check the vendor’s page and tell us.

table.title: Comparison table

unbit.setup: No kernel extension or macFUSE. Needs Full Disk Access and a one-time approval of a read helper

iboysoft.price: Paid – subscription or one-time licence; check current pricing. Trial can browse and preview only
iboysoft.setup: Finder mode needs a system extension (Reduced Security on Apple silicon). A File Manager mode works without it

hasleo.price: Paid – one-time licence; check current pricing
hasleo.setup: On Apple silicon the vendor describes Reduced Security and allowing kernel extensions. Needs Full Disk Access

uubyte.price: Paid – 1-year plan or lifetime licence; check current pricing
uubyte.write: Read; write access can be enabled after unlocking
uubyte.silicon: Yes – the vendor has an Apple silicon guide
uubyte.setup: The vendor’s Apple silicon guide covers Full Disk Access, kernel extensions, a system extension update and a restart

anylinuxfs.write: Read-write by default; read-only can be selected
anylinuxfs.setup: No kernel extension. Runs a lightweight virtual machine and shares the drive over NFS. Installed with Homebrew
anylinuxfs.unlock: Password, or the recovery key used as passphrase

parallels.price: Paid – subscription or one-time (Standard). Windows licence not included
parallels.write: Whatever Windows allows, so read and write
parallels.setup: No BitLocker driver on macOS. The USB drive is connected to the virtual machine and is then not visible on the Mac
parallels.unlock: Password or recovery key, entered in Windows

table.note: Based on vendor pages checked on 1 October 2026. Prices, features and system requirements change, so check each vendor before you buy. The sourced detail for every product is on its comparison page.

unbit.bestFor: reading files from a BitLocker drive and copying them to your Mac.
unbit.text: Unbit is a free menu bar app. It detects the external drive, asks for the password or recovery key and mounts the drive in Finder as read-only. Everything is decrypted on your Mac, and it uses no kernel extension or macFUSE. Because it never writes, it also can’t damage or change the drive.
pros: Free, with no licence key or trial limits
No kernel extension, macFUSE or lowered startup security
Universal app for Apple silicon and Intel
Opens with a password or the 48-digit recovery key
Runs locally, no accounts or tracking
cons: Read-only by design: you can’t save, delete or add files on the drive
Can’t encrypt drives or change BitLocker settings
External drives only, not internal disks

iboysoft.bestFor: people who want to write to BitLocker drives from the Mac, or encrypt drives on macOS.
iboysoft.text: iBoysoft BitLocker for Mac is a commercial app with read-write access. It has two modes: a File Manager mode and a Volume Mounter mode that mounts the drive in Finder. It can also encrypt drives with BitLocker.
pros: Read and write access
Can also encrypt drives with BitLocker
A File Manager mode that works without a system extension
Supports M-series and Intel Macs
cons: Paid; the trial only browses and previews files
Finder mode needs a system extension, and on Apple silicon the vendor documents Reduced Security
Activation needs internet access, according to the vendor

hasleo.bestFor: people who want one paid tool to mount, encrypt and decrypt BitLocker drives.
hasleo.text: Hasleo BitLocker Anywhere for Mac mounts BitLocker drives read-write or read-only and can also encrypt and decrypt them. The vendor lists it at a lower price than the other paid apps at the time of writing; check current pricing.
pros: Read-write or read-only mounting
Can encrypt and decrypt drives and change the password
Lists Intel and Apple silicon support
cons: On Apple silicon the setup involves Reduced Security and kernel extensions, according to the vendor’s forum
We couldn’t verify the limits of its free/trial version

uubyte.bestFor: people who mostly read but want the option to write after unlocking.
uubyte.text: UUByte BitLocker Geeker is a paid app. After unlocking you can view and copy files, and write access is switched on with an Enable Write button, according to the vendor.
pros: Optional write access
Keychain auto-unlock
The vendor documents the steps for M-series Macs
cons: The Apple silicon steps include kernel extensions and a restart
Not read-only unless you leave write access off

anylinuxfs.bestFor: people who are comfortable in Terminal and want a free read-write option.
anylinuxfs.text: anylinuxfs is a free, open-source command-line tool that mounts Linux-supported file systems, including BitLocker drives, on Apple silicon Macs. It runs a lightweight virtual machine and shares the drive to your Mac over NFS.
pros: Free and open source
Read-write, with read-only mounting selectable
No kernel extension and no lowered system security
Also handles ext4, btrfs, LUKS and more
cons: Command line and Homebrew; not a point-and-click app
The drive appears as a network drive, and the project lists known limitations

parallels.bestFor: people who already run Windows on their Mac.
parallels.text: Parallels Desktop is a virtualization app, not a BitLocker tool. You connect the external drive to a Windows virtual machine and unlock it with Windows’ own BitLocker support. It works, but it is the largest setup of the six.
pros: Full Windows behaviour for the drive, including writing
Also runs Windows apps
No BitLocker driver needed on macOS
cons: Needs a Windows installation and licence, plus disk space and memory
While attached to the virtual machine, the drive isn’t visible on the Mac

pick.title: Which should you choose?
paragraphs: If you only need the files – a USB stick from a colleague, an old backup drive, a disk from a Windows PC – start with the simplest tool that does that. [Unbit](home) is free, installs like any Mac app and keeps the drive untouched. Its limit is the point: it can’t write, so there is nothing to undo.

If you need to write to the drive, pick a read-write option: one of the paid Mac apps, anylinuxfs if you like Terminal, or Windows in a virtual machine. Compare price, setup and Apple silicon support on each product’s [comparison page](alternatives), and check current pricing before you buy.

Whatever you choose, keep the password or the 48-digit recovery key safe – without one of them nobody can open the drive. New to this? Start with [How to open a BitLocker drive on a Mac](open), or see [BitLocker recovery key on Mac](recovery) if you lost the password.

faq.q: What is the best BitLocker for Mac?
faq.a: It depends on the job. For reading files and copying them to your Mac, a free read-only tool like [Unbit](home) is enough. If you need to write to the drive, look at the paid read-write apps, anylinuxfs or Windows in a virtual machine.

faq.q: Is there a free BitLocker for Mac?
faq.a: Yes. Unbit is free and read-only, and anylinuxfs is free, open source and read-write but runs from Terminal on Apple silicon Macs. The other apps in this comparison are paid.
No. macOS has no built-in BitLocker support. Its own encryption is FileVault, which is a different technology.

faq.q: Can I write to a BitLocker drive on a Mac?
faq.a: Yes with some tools – the paid apps, anylinuxfs or Windows in a virtual machine. Not with Unbit, which is read-only by design.

faq.q: Do these tools work on Apple silicon Macs?
faq.a: Most list support for both Apple silicon and Intel; anylinuxfs supports Apple silicon only. Setup differs a lot, so check each vendor’s documentation.

faq.q: Is it safe to open a BitLocker drive on a Mac?
faq.a: Opening a drive read-only can’t change it. See [Is BitLocker on Mac safe?](safe) for what Unbit does with your password and files.
